claim_1.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood cells from 92 healthy male adults before vaccination and on days 1, 3, and 14 after trivalent influenza vaccination (day 0), using linear mixed-effects ANOVA and pathway enrichment analysis, showed that the largest transcriptional changes occurred 1 day after vaccination (day 1), with early upregulation of interferon-inducible genes including IFIT1, MX1, and IRF9, JAK/STAT and NFκB signaling, and antigen-processing/presentation genes, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: We identified expression changes in 4740 transcripts (Dataset 1) after imposing a FDR cutoff of 0.01 on the P value for the day effect.
The maximum expression change occurred on day 1, while day 14 had the greatest number of genes with maximum expression values.

The top 1% differentially expressed genes included interferon-inducible genes (eg, IFIT1, MX1, and IRF9), the signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) gene family, genes with ribosomal functions (eg, RPL7, RGS18, and RPS27), and genes with unclear functions (eg, WARS and the family of guanylate-binding proteins).
As expected, the early phase of transcriptional activation was marked by upregulation of genes involved in multiple immune processes.

Activation of antigen processing and presentation is implied by the increased expression of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) Class I genes (eg, GO:002474). Associations were most significant for the interferon response pathway (GO:0005062, GO:0034341, and GO:0034340) when compared with other cytokines.

claim_2.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood cells from 92 healthy male adults before vaccination and on days 1, 3, and 14 after trivalent influenza vaccination (day 0), using pathway enrichment analysis, showed a late transcriptional program with increased expression of genes involved in macromolecule biosynthesis, cellular protein metabolism, RNA metabolic processing, and regulation of antiapoptosis at day 14 compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: In contrast, the late vaccine response was characterized by increased detection of transcripts for genes involved in intracellular processes suggestive of active cellular proliferation, including macromolecule biosynthesis (eg, GO:0009059), cellular protein metabolism (eg, GO:0044267), RNA metabolic processing (eg, GO:0016070), and regulation of antiapoptosis (GO:0045767).

claim_3.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood cells from 92 healthy male adults before vaccination and on days 1, 3, and 14 after trivalent influenza vaccination (day 0), using correlation with the titer response index, showed that a 494-transcript signature correlated with antibody response magnitude, with STAT1 expression increasing most prominently on day 1 in high responders and E2F2 being more strongly downregulated on day 3 in high responders compared to low responders.

sources.quote: We found that the abundance level of 494 transcripts significantly correlated with the TRI (Dataset 8).

Two opposing expression trends influenced the magnitude of the antibody response, and the maximum effects were observed at specific time points as illustrated by the genes STAT1 and E2F2 in Figure 2B.

claim_4.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood cells from 92 healthy male adults before vaccination and on days 1 and 3 after trivalent influenza vaccination (day 0), using cross-validated linear prediction with a subset of transcripts including STAT1, IRF9, SPI1, CD74, HLA-E, TNFSF13B, PRDX2, PRDX3, E2F2, PTEN, and ITGB1, showed that early residual expression values predicted the observed antibody response index and recategorized the highest and lowest responders into the appropriate groups compared to the opposite response group.

sources.quote: We show that the residual expression values on days 1 and 3 are predictive of the observed TRI for each individual and, more importantly, that the cross-validated predicted TRI recategorized the highest and lowest responders into the appropriate groups (Figure 2D).

claim_5.claim: Hemagglutination inhibition analysis of serum from 92 healthy male adults before vaccination and on days 14 and 28 after trivalent influenza vaccination (day 0), together with neutralization assay data summarized in the titer response index, showed that antibody titers generally plateaued after day 14 and that the titer response index was positively associated with the rise in HAI titer compared to prevaccination baseline.

sources.quote: Antibody titers were measured by both hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) and neutralization assays. The titer results from these assays were strongly correlated, and the titers generally plateaued after day 14.
The TRI and rise in HAI titer for the 92 individuals show a significant positive relationship (r2 5 0.4585).

claim_6.claim: Neutralization assay analysis of serum from 92 healthy male adults before vaccination and on days 14 and 28 after trivalent influenza vaccination (day 0), compared with hemagglutination inhibition results, showed that neutralization titers were strongly correlated with HAI titers and contributed to a trimodal titer response index that classified individuals as high, intermediate, and low responders compared to the rest of the cohort.

sources.quote: Antibody titers were measured by both hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) and neutralization assays. The titer results from these assays were strongly correlated, and the titers generally plateaued after day 14.

Interestingly, the distribution of the TRI scores is trimodal, facilitating an unbiased classification of individuals as high, intermediate, and low vaccine responders (Figure 2A), depending on where the individual’s TRI falls under this distribution.

claim_7.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood cells from high and low vaccine responders after trivalent influenza vaccination, using Gene Ontology and network analysis, showed that high responders preferentially upregulated interferon-response and antigen-presentation pathways, including interferon signaling, activation of IRF by cytosolic pattern recognition receptors, and antigen presentation, compared to low responders.

sources.quote: Content analysis of the genes that were upregulated in the high-responder group showed enrichment of GO categories involved in cellular immune responses, most notably the interferon response and antigen presentation pathways (Figure 3A and Datasets 9, 10).
Genes within the interferon response pathway were highly upregulated in the high-responder group (Figure 3B).
